A grotto is a type of cavern, often closely associated with water. Grottos are a prominent feature of many religious and garden settings as places of contemplation. One of the most impressive collection of grottos is the Longmen Grottos in Luoyang, China, which houses tens of thousands of Buddhas, stelae, and inscriptions.

The Place of Truth was an ancient artisan village which housed the labourers and crafstmen that built the Valley of Kings, cutting and decorating the tombs of countless Pharoahs. In addition to being a vast public works project in its own right, the Place of Truth was also the site of history's first recorded worker's strike, when the workers performed a sit-in strike in protest over the lack of rations and supplies for their compensation.

The Akapana is not like other Founder Belief National Wonders, because it can be purchased with Faith immediately upon founding, rather than being unlocked after a certain proportion of the population follows your religion. However, the Akapana does not allow you to found immediately after building it. Instead, you need to spend faith to upgrade your Akapana by performing Challa Rituals. Each Challa Ritual gets you closer to reforming your religion, and adds yields to the Akapana, making it a powerful economic boost to your empire.

On the shores of Lake Titicaca are the remains of one of the most powerful and influential cultures to appear in the Andean mountains: Tiwanaku. Long before the Incan Empire, the priests and nobles of Tiwanaku cultivated a hegemony over modern day Bolivia and northern Chile, based solely on cultural and religious influence. Within Tiwanaku was a sprawling complex of temples and courtyards for various rituals and rites, but the greatest of them all was the Akapana, a gargantuan manmade stepped pyramid in the shape of a modified Andean Cross.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Akapana's resemblance to the nearby mountains was not an accident, just as the mountains surrounding Lake Titicaca feed the great lake with their spring water, the Akapana is believed to have collected rainwater on its flat upper surface and funneled it into a depression at the centre. The centre of the pyramid contained a hole, filled with loose stones, which permitted water to drain out of the Akapana's center, and down into a moat surrounding the temple complex. Thus, the Akapana would have been seen as a holy mountain in its own right, blessing the city with its water. The act of pouring and collecting water and sacred drinks was central to many Andean religions, which presented gifts to the earth by pouring out drinks or burying meals and trinkets.

The Challa rituals are a central part of worship to Pachamama, the earth deity of many Pre-Columbian Andean cultures. Each day, priests would prepare a cup of chicha -- a kind of beer made from corn -- and spill a small amount as an offering to Pachamama before drinking the rest. We do not know for sure where the ritual originated, but the city of Tiwanaku contained one of the oldest and grandest temple complexes where these ceremonies took place.

If you have adopted the Libations founder belief, use your faith to perform Challa rituals which make your Akapana wonder stronger. Can perform a [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Max of 25[ENDCOLOR] Challa Rituals.

Sweat Lodge

A sweat lodge is a small domed hut used by various North American Indigenous cultures for dry heat sessions, similar to a sauna. The religious traditions surrounding these sessions, often referred to simpy as 'sweats', differ greatly between nations, but often include purification and initiation rituals.

Can only be built in cities following a religion with the Sweat Lodges belief. Construct this building by purchasing it with [ICON_PEACE] Faith. This building and makes your units heal faster in the city, and boosts nearby Camps and Plantations.

Dar-e Mehr

The Zoroastrian Fire Temples, or Dar-e Mehr, were the centers of Persian religious life. Water and fire are honoured as the main components of ritual purification in Zoroatrianism. Fire, Atar, is held in special regard as the manifestation of Ahura Mazda, the singular creator god of Zoroastrianism. The altar inside the Dar-e Mehr is kept perpetually lit and purifying ash from the fire is used in the priests' various rituals.
